# E7 — the gate as a classifier: every saved candidate judged again by the harness, each check on its own, DataRaceBench as the outside ground truth for races

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

How often did the gate accept a wrong change or refuse a right one, what did each check decide alone, and how much rests on the second input? (RQ2, C2, H3) — on the 3,034 candidates saved in E1-v6 and E2-v6b, the 248 directives of the six no-model draws of DiscoPoP alone, and DataRaceBench's labelled kernels. No model call.

## Result in one paragraph

Reopened 11 Nov (the author: "do this one"); registered as it runs in the record's row of that date; the pilot and the main runs are registered below. No result yet.

## Change-log rows that name these runs (§6)

| Date | Repo | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-11 | plan | **E7 reopened and registered as it will run — the gate as a classifier. The author (11 Nov): "do this one … come back to me when everything is done if you need something from me go with the recommended". Written before any E7 run; no model call anywhere in it.** *Why now:* the thesis states that the gate let nothing unusable through, but not how often it refuses a right candidate or which check catches what the others miss (its §7.2); the archive answers neither — 576 of the 1,389 distinct programs the gate judged in E1-v6 and E2-v6b were refused and never judged by anything else, and 693 were accepted on the way without being a trial's final file. *What stands from the design of 9 Oct (the row of that date):* Part A's two corpora, the judge (J1 the harness's verification as in every trial; J2 ThreadSanitizer with archer at the verification size, 12 threads, 3 runs, for a program that holds a directive), the definition of a wrong candidate (J1 fails or J2 reports a race while its base passes; a candidate on a base that fails is counted apart; a candidate refused before a program exists enters no rate, only the agreement that the judge's build fails too), the read-outs R1 (gate × judge), R2 (each check on its own) and R3 (the second input), the pilot of 40 candidates with a fixed seed, and Part B (DataRaceBench) after Part A. *Built today (Mac, text only):* `tools/gate_study.py` (`corpus`, `judge`, `checks`); the corpora rebuilt from the archive into `results/E07_gate_as_classifier/corpus/a1` and `corpus/a2` — **A1** 3,034 candidates in 431 trials, 3,023 rebuilt, 1,389 distinct programs (506 with a directive; 813 accepted, 576 refused), **A2** 248 candidates in 114 trials, all rebuilt, 187 distinct programs (108 accepted, 79 refused) — the pre-flight's counts of 9 Oct exactly; the 11 candidates of A1 that cannot be rebuilt are accepted directives of the final pass and are listed in `corpus.json` (`not_rebuilt`), left out by name; every trial's `original/` equals today's package byte for byte (436 of 436), so `verify-source` judges each candidate against the data the gate saw. Tooling tried on the Mac on six candidates (no result read from it). *Decisions taken as the recommended option, each a deviation from the 9 Oct design:* **(1) A1 is the corpus as it stood on 9 Oct.** One run has been registered in E1-v6 since (`e1v6c_v8_agent`, 10 Oct, 88 candidates): it is left out by name, because the gate that judged it already held Fix 105 and the design pools only candidates one version of the gate judged. **(2) R3 is the replay** — the wrong candidates only the perturbed input refuses, on every saved candidate; the 12 model trials of the first plan are not run (the design offered this "if the author agrees"). **(3) The gate that is replayed is today's** (44fbeefad): since the corpus was judged it changed in four commits (Fix 105 the dependence stage's line numbers, Fix 108, Fix 113 with `--exact-repeat`, off, Fix 114 the judge's timer check); none touches a stage that is replayed, and the fidelity table lists every disagreement between the replayed whole gate and the recorded verdict. **(4) Each check alone** is run by calling the gate's own `validate()` with the other checks switched off by its arguments (ThreadSanitizer alone: no reference, no matrix; the matrix alone: the sanitizer's run skipped, the matrix's own verdict — hard or soft — taken from `stress_schedules`; each input alone: one reference pair); no switch is added to the gate, so the agent's code does not change. Run-dependent checks three times, as designed. **(5) R4 is not run.** Its question — should the dependence check read the profile at the profile's line numbers — was decided on 9 Oct (Fix 105) with its own count from the archive (the correction row of that date); the check refused no candidate of A1 and one of A2 (the `mvt` directive, a known false refusal), and that candidate is read through the judge and the other checks like every other. A fresh DiscoPoP profile of every profiled text would be a new draw of DiscoPoP, not a replay of the check. **(6) R5 is limited to the named cases the two corpora hold** (the `s281` clause refusal in A1; DiscoPoP's directives on `hotspot`, `mvt` and `floyd-warshall` in A2, where present); programs from earlier experiments are not judged again. *The judge is today's harness* (`cli.verify` at 44fbeefad); a trial's own verdict on its final program, where the candidate is one, is shown beside the judge's as its repeatability. *Definitions, fixed now:* J1 right = the harness's outcome FASTER, parallel-not-faster, parallel-speed-not-measurable, changed-not-parallel or no-change; wrong = BROKEN; VERIFY_FAILED = the program does not build at the verification size (agreement for a candidate the gate refused at `compile` or `openmp_compile`, wrong otherwise); SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED = the candidate changed the measuring code, counted apart as not judgeable. Speed is not part of right or wrong. Rates with 95 % Wilson intervals, per candidate, per distinct program and per loop; every false accept and every false refusal listed by name and read. *Runs, registered in group E7 before they start:* the pilot `e7_pilot` (judge) and `e7_pilot_checks` (launcher `analysis/e7_pilot.sh`, one 12-core group) — it counts as passed when every program of the draw has an outcome from the harness and a race verdict where it holds a directive, and every disagreement between the replayed gate and the recorded verdict has been read and explained; its seconds per candidate fix the main runs' duration. Then `e7_a1_judge_1` … `e7_a1_judge_4` and `e7_a1_checks` on four groups, and `e7_a2_judge_1`, `e7_a2_judge_2` and `e7_a2_checks` on two (A2 holds PolyBench and the applications; launcher `analysis/e7_main.sh`). Part B gets its own row before it runs. *Expectations, unchanged from 9 Oct:* no false accept among programs that were a trial's final file; possible ones among candidates accepted on the way; the largest class of false refusals an output comparison that refuses a rewrite which only reorders floating-point additions; unique catches for ThreadSanitizer and for the perturbed input, few for the schedule matrix. *What decides what:* nothing changes a result of E1-v6 or E2-v6b; the numbers enter the thesis as the gate's measured error | Plan, E7 reopened |
